## Claude review

**Verdict:** changes_requested

I read every changed file in full against the base `origin/ai-implement/feature/aii-1298`: CLAUDE.md, docs/review-fix-rail.md, src/__tests__/restate/late-external-review.restate.test.ts, src/__tests__/review-fix-production-delegation.test.ts, src/__tests__/runner-callback.test.ts, src/index.ts, src/log.ts, src/restate/late-external-review.ts, src/restate/review-fix-production.ts, and src/runner-callback.ts — and followed the new code to its callers (src/restate/review-fix-attempt.ts's `ctx.run("apply-approval-once", ...)`, index.ts's wiring of `submitLateExternalReview`/`lateExternalReviewSubmitHook`, and `createLateExternalReviewIngressClient`'s submit semantics).

The diff correctly implements the directly-reviewed acceptance criteria from the prior review round (AC1-AC4): a succeeded review-fix attempt's approval effect now submits `LateExternalReview` with `gapFill:true` for the PR's latest implementation/gap-analysis row, keyed `<dispatchId>-<attemptId>` so it doesn't collide with an already-superseded workflow on the same row, stamps nothing directly, and the Restate tests for approve/changes_requested/duplicate-submit all check out against the workflow implementation.

The second commit ("fix: address review feedback (iter 1)") was meant to close the previously-flagged gap — reusing the AII-1304 poll sweep so a Restate-not-ready moment at finalize time doesn't leave a human as the only fallback. It adds a new `attempt_review_pending` table (src/log.ts) and a second loop in `resubmitPendingGapFillReviews` (src/runner-callback.ts) that resubmits and then unconditionally clears each pending row after any non-throwing `submit` call. That's the bug: the production submit hook (`createLateExternalReviewSubmitHook` / `createLateExternalReviewIngressClient`, src/restate/late-external-review.ts) resolves normally even when the real Restate call failed (`unavailable`), so the sweep cannot distinguish a genuine success from a silent failure, and deletes the only retry record either way. Since the initial submit also runs inside a Restate-journaled step and therefore fires exactly once per attempt, this sweep is the *only* remaining retry path — so a single transient failure during the sweep permanently loses the attempt's approval submission, with nothing left to notice or retry it. This reintroduces, silently, precisely the human-dependency problem the ticket sets out to remove, and it diverges from the pre-existing AII-1304 loop's design, which is immune to this because it re-derives "still pending" from `dispatch_log`'s own `approved`/`conclusion` columns rather than a side table cleared on faith. I flagged this as blocking, plus two related minor points (a guaranteed extra round-trip on the happy path, and a test gap that doesn't model the failure-that-looks-like-success case).

### Findings

- **[blocking]** (src/runner-callback.ts:1620): The new attempt-review resubmit loop clears its only retry record on any non-throwing `submit` call, but the production `submit` hook can resolve normally even when the actual Restate submission failed — so a transient failure during the sweep permanently drops the retry with no further attempt, silently reintroducing the exact "PR waits for a person" gap this ticket exists to close.

Trace: `submitLateReviewForAttempt` (src/restate/review-fix-production.ts:97-116) runs inside `ctx.run("apply-approval-once", ...)` in src/restate/review-fix-attempt.ts:276 — a Restate journaled step, so it executes exactly once per attempt no matter how many times the workflow replays. Its `recordPendingAttemptReview` call (review-fix-production.ts:112) is therefore the only chance to seed a retry record; after that, `attempt_review_pending` + the poll sweep in runner-callback.ts:1620-1631 is the *sole* remaining retry path.

That sweep calls `opts.submit(...)` and, on any resolve (no throw), immediately calls `clearPendingAttemptReview` (runner-callback.ts:1626) and counts it as submitted. In production `opts.submit` is `lateExternalReviewSubmitHook` → `createLateExternalReviewSubmitHook` (src/restate/late-external-review.ts:346-357), which never throws: it either logs-and-returns when Restate isn't ready, or awaits `ingress.submit(input)`, whose own docstring says "Never throws: a connection error or timeout resolves `unavailable`" (late-external-review.ts:317-333). So a genuine `unavailable` outcome (sidecar reports ready via `restateReady()`, but the actual HTTP/gRPC call to ingress times out or 5xxs) is indistinguishable from a real `accepted`/`conflict` from the caller's perspective — the `catch` branch at runner-callback.ts:1628 is effectively dead code in production, and the pending row is deleted regardless of whether Restate ever actually ran the workflow.

Contrast with the pre-existing AII-1304 loop immediately above it (runner-callback.ts:1605-1617): that one never explicitly "clears" anything — it relies on `getGapFillRowsAwaitingLateReview` re-querying `dispatch_log`'s own `approved`/`conclusion` columns, so a submission that silently failed naturally reappears on the next poll within the 24h window. The new attempt-review path discards that self-healing property by keying retry-or-not off whether the hook call merely resolved rather than off any confirmed outcome.

docs/review-fix-rail.md:232's new section compounds this by asserting the row "clears it once the submit is accepted" — that is not what the code does; it clears on any resolved call, accepted or not.

Failure scenario: Restate sidecar reports itself ready, but the ingress call to submit `LateExternalReview` for a review-fix attempt's PR times out once during the poll sweep. `ingress.submit` catches the error and returns `unavailable`; the hook logs it and resolves; the sweep sees no exception, clears the `attempt_review_pending` row, and increments `submitted`. The workflow was never actually started at Restate, so `LateExternalReview` never runs, the PR's run row never gets its approval mark, and there is no code path left that will retry — the PR sits exactly like it did before this PR, except now nothing is pending and nothing signals the operator that a retry is needed.
- **[minor]** (src/restate/review-fix-production.ts:111): Even on the common, fully successful path (Restate ready, submit genuinely accepted), `submitLateReviewForAttempt` has no way to clear the `attempt_review_pending` row it just wrote, because `recordPendingAttemptReview` (line 112) runs before the outcome of `submit` is known and the hook's `Promise<void>` signature never surfaces that outcome back to the caller. The row is only ever removed later by the poll sweep's resubmit, which then predictably gets a 409 `conflict` from the already-consumed workflow key (since the key is `<dispatchId>-<attemptId>` and Restate enforces one-shot submission per key). So every single successful attempt approval generates one guaranteed, unnecessary duplicate submit call + log line on the next poll tick, purely to re-discover something that already succeeded. This is wasteful but harmless on its own (the 409 is swallowed); it's the same root cause as the blocking finding above — the design has no real success signal to act on — so fixing that will likely fix this too.
- **[minor]** (src/__tests__/runner-callback.test.ts:1348): The new test ("re-submits a pending review-fix attempt with its attemptId once, then clears it") only exercises `submit = vi.fn(async () => {})`, i.e. a mock that always genuinely succeeds. It never models the realistic shape the production hook actually produces — a resolved promise that corresponds to an `unavailable` (failed) submission — so it can't catch the blocking issue above: that the sweep clears the pending row even when the real submission didn't go through. A test that passes a `submit` resolving normally but recording that it internally hit "unavailable" (or, more simply, asserts the row is retained unless some success signal is observed) would have caught this.
